findings.issue: The open-redirect test can never fail for the most important hostile value. `toHaveTextContent(string)` checks for a substring. If safeNext were removed, '//evil.example/x' would produce '/login?error=AUTH_OIDC_LOGIN_FAILED&next=%2F%2Fevil.example%2Fx', and that still contains the expected '...&next=%2F', so the test passes. In other words, the protocol-relative open-redirect guard that this test claims to pin is not covered. Only the 'https://evil.example' and 'javascript:alert(1)' cases would catch a regression, because their encoded form does not start with %2F.
findings.fix: Assert the whole value. Either check `whereText()` with `toBe('/login?error=AUTH_OIDC_LOGIN_FAILED&next=%2F')`, or parse the query and assert `new URLSearchParams(...).get('next') === '/'`. Also assert that the stored key is removed. Apply the same exact match to the other callback tests (error, mfaToken, anonymous, stored-path) so that a value with extra appended text cannot pass.

findings.issue: The hostile literal '/\evil.example' is written as '/\evil.example' with a single backslash in a single-quoted JS string. In JS '\e' is just 'e', so the runtime value is '/evil.example'. That is a legitimate same-origin path, and safeNext correctly lets it through. The test then 'passes' only because of the substring match above. The backslash bypass that safeNext explicitly guards against (next.startsWith('/\\')) is therefore never exercised. The test is mislabelled: it claims a hostile value is rejected when it actually passes a benign one.
findings.fix: Use '/\\evil.example' (an escaped backslash) or String.raw`/\evil.example`. Together with the exact assertion, this makes the case real. Optionally add '/\t/evil.example' and '%2F%2Fevil.example' as extra hostile inputs.

findings.issue: lib/redirect is fully mocked, so the button test only checks that the raw prop is passed through. Nothing in this change (and no redirect.test.ts exists) checks that rememberPostLoginRedirect/safeNext refuse to store '//host', '/\\host', 'https://...' or 'javascript:'. The write-side sanitisation of the post-login redirect therefore has no direct test.
findings.fix: Add src/lib/redirect.test.ts with table cases for safeNext (accept '/a?b=1'; reject '', null, 'a', '//x', '/\\x', 'https://x', 'javascript:x'). Also test that rememberPostLoginRedirect stores the sanitised value and that takePostLoginRedirect consumes the key. Alternatively, add one unmocked button test that checks what lands in sessionStorage for a hostile next.

findings.issue: PRODUCTION issue (out of scope for this test-only change). The Idempotency-Key is thrown away on any ApiError with status < 500. That includes 409 (for example, an idempotency 'request in progress' or conflict reply), 408 and 429. For these, the server may already have processed the first request or may still be processing it. Retrying with a fresh key could then create a second order or charge. The new test pins 400 leading to a new key (correct), and 5xx/network leading to the same key (correct), but these ambiguous statuses are not considered.
findings.fix: Separate follow-up: keep the key for 408, 409 (unless the code is a known business rejection such as OUT_OF_STOCK or PAYMENT_METHOD_UNAVAILABLE) and 429, and rotate it only for definitive validation or business rejections. Add tests for those statuses at the same time.

summary: This is a test-only change: no production code, no new dependencies, and no secrets in the fixtures (the name, address, 'mfa-123' and publicKey 'k' are all synthetic). The checkout tests pin the money-relevant behaviour well. The place payloads are asserted with exact toEqual and never carry client totals or prices. The PaymentPanel view shows the server's totalAmount (1290.50 vs the client's 1290). Double-click protection is pinned. Idempotency-Key handling is pinned correctly: same key on 5xx and network retry, new key on 4xx and on a changed request shape, distinct keys per page. That guards against double charges. The test that the mfaToken takes precedence over authenticated is correct, and so is the test that the callback ignores a ?next= query parameter. However, the callback's open-redirect tests, the main security assertion of this change, are largely vacuous. A substring toHaveTextContent match means that a stored '//evil.example/x' would pass even with safeNext deleted. The '/\evil.example' case is mis-escaped into a benign '/evil.example', so the backslash bypass is never exercised. The Google button test mocks lib/redirect, and no redirect unit test exists, so write-side sanitisation is also untested. The production safeNext/takePostLoginRedirect logic itself looks sound for react-router navigation. One minor PRODUCTION observation, outside this change: CheckoutPage rotates the Idempotency-Key for all 4xx, including the ambiguous 408, 409 and 429. Request changes: make the hostile-redirect assertions exact and fix the escaping, then this can be approved.
